newsitem.title: CHINA: China grants France's Banque Indosuez yuan licence.
newsitem.headline: China grants France's Banque Indosuez yuan licence.

text.p: France's Banque Indosuez has become the ninth foreign bank in Shanghai to be granted approval to do local currency business, a bank official said on Thursday.
The official said he expected the bank to start handling yuan loans and deposits by the end of June.
Several other foreign banks started limited yuan business last month.
Under the rules laid down by the Chinese central bank, foreign banks are basically only allowed to do yuan business with foreign-funded firms based in Shanghai.

They are required to move their main branches to the Pudong district to the east of Shanghai's city centre before starting local currency transactions. Shanghai's city government wants Pudong to become a major financial centre.
